author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Rivers across England are facing widespread chemical and sewage pollution, raising concerns about the future of freshwater ecosystems and the impact on wildlife.

Al Jazeera's Camille Nedelec reports on the scale of the crisis, including findings that all English rivers fail chemical standards and that 85% are contaminated by parasiticides linked to pet flea treatments.

Chris Coode, chief executive of Thames21, explains how climate change is worsening the problem. Rising water temperatures and droughts can intensify the effects of pollution, putting additional pressure on already vulnerable ecosystems.

Despite the challenges, Coode says nature can recover if the sources of pollution are removed.

The report also examines proposed reforms to the UK water industry, including changes intended to strengthen accountability and give local leaders greater powers to hold water companies responsible for pollution.

description: A cyberattack has disrupted hundreds of supermarkets across France, reportedly causing refrigeration temperatures to rise to 50 degrees Celsius, sparking fires in several stores and spoiling large quantities of food. That's in violation of the US-brokered ceasefire that came into effect just over a year ago.
The so-called “Yellow Line” separates the Israeli military zone from the rest of the Strip.
Palestinian families are being displaced again as the expanded boundary now places them within the Israeli-controlled zone.
 
Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud reports from Gaza City.

description:
Israel's relentless bombardment of Gaza has left much of the territory's cultural heritage in ruins.
Museums, archaeological sites and centuries-old landmarks have been damaged or destroyed.
Palestinians say it's an attempt to erase their history and identity.
But amid the destruction, archaeologists and young volunteers are working to salvage what remains piece by piece - preserving a heritage that spans thousands of years.

Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reports from Khan Younis, southern Gaza.

description:
Israel is expanding its military control inside the Gaza Strip despite the US-brokered ceasefire, with new forced evacuation orders raising fears among Palestinians already displaced by the war. Nearly two-thirds of Gaza is now reported to lie beyond the so-called yellow line, the boundary established under US President Donald Trump's 20-point peace plan.

Al Jazeera's Ibrahim Al-Khalili reports from Gaza City, where Palestinians face renewed displacement as the Israeli military expands its control. The report examines the impact of shifting boundaries and continuing Israeli attacks, including a strike on a residential building in Deir el-Balah that left widespread destruction and forced families to sleep outdoors.

A professor of international law also questions whether Trump's peace plan can end Israel's occupation, citing the International Court of Justice's 2024 advisory opinion on the occupied Palestinian territory.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Al Jazeera interviews Trita Parsi, Executive Vice President of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, about Iran’s mediation efforts in Yemen and escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington.

Parsi explains why Iran is seeking to prevent a wider regional war, while stressing that Yemen’s Houthi movement, also known as Ansar Allah, operates independently and does not always follow Tehran’s advice. He also examines Saudi-Iranian normalisation, the possibility of further US escalation after the midterm elections, and the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz.

Parsi warns that the relative calm in the Strait of Hormuz may not last, raising concerns about the risk of renewed regional conflict.
